name: Block starts and short drives
coaching_cues: Aggressive push out of the blocks; stay low through the drive; strike under the hip

name: Hill repeats 60-100m
coaching_cues: Lean from the ankles into the hill; powerful arm drive; full push through the ground

name: Block starts to 30-40m
coaching_cues: Own the first three steps; gradual rise, no standing up at 10m; relaxed shoulders

name: Sled or harness pulls + free sprints
coaching_cues: Resisted reps should look like sprinting, not marching; free reps right after feel the contrast

name: Fly runs (20m build + fly zone)
coaching_cues: Tall and relaxed in the fly zone; fast turnover without reaching; front-side mechanics

name: Ins-and-outs 30-30-30
coaching_cues: Blast-float-blast: float means hold speed with less effort, not slow down; re-attack the last 30

name: Light fly runs or block starts
coaching_cues: Sharp, not exhausting; stop while it still feels fast; nothing to failure this phase

name: Short speed endurance 120-150m
coaching_cues: Fast but controlled off the turn; hold form as fatigue builds; finish tall

name: Split runs 120m + 80m
rest: 60-90 sec inside set, 8 min between sets
coaching_cues: Second rep starts tired on purpose; re-accelerate instead of surviving

name: Speed endurance fast 150m
coaching_cues: Race effort with discipline; the last 50m is a form test, not a grit test

name: 200m + 120m at race effort
coaching_cues: Run the 200 like a final; the 120 after it teaches finishing under fatigue

name: Light speed endurance 120m
coaching_cues: Smooth 90 percent; if it is not smooth, strides only today

name: 100m accelerations to 90%
coaching_cues: Build through the rep; top speed without strain; low end of the speed endurance ladder

name: 300m build-ups (200m runners)
coaching_cues: Build the rep in thirds; last 100 is controlled aggression; early-phase only for 200m group

name: 8 x 200m fast and relaxed
coaching_cues: Fast and relaxed is the whole point; if form goes, the rep is over

name: Extensive tempo 100s
coaching_cues: Relaxed rhythm; nasal breathing early reps; this builds the base that protects speed days

name: Tempo 100s + low plyos
coaching_cues: Tempo first, plyos after while warm; keep plyo contacts low and springy

name: Fartlek up to 30 min
coaching_cues: Surges are strong strides, not sprints; keep the jog honest between them

name: 400m fartlek reps
coaching_cues: Each 400 mixes walk, jog, stride, and a sprint 100; smooth transitions, no hero reps

name: 100m race modeling: blocks to 60m
coaching_cues: Drive 0-30, transition 30-60; rehearse the race in segments, then trust it

name: 200m curve modeling: blocks to 80-120m
coaching_cues: Attack the curve with lean; lane discipline is a skill, practice it; float, do not force

name: Broken runs (200 / jog / 200)
rest: jog across the field between segments
coaching_cues: Second fast segment starts on tired legs like a real final; variants: 300+jog+100, 100+jog+300

name: 150m race simulations
coaching_cues: 100m push, 50m power; this is the 200m race in miniature

name: Pre-meet primer: light starts and strides
coaching_cues: Touch speed, do not train it; leave the track feeling fast; mobility after

name: Base weights + circuit
coaching_cues: Moderate loads, clean reps; core and mini-band work in the circuit; build capacity, not soreness

name: Heavy weights (speed phase)
coaching_cues: Heavier but never grinding; bar speed matters; pair with easy tempo for recovery

name: Low-impact plyos
coaching_cues: Quiet landings; spring off the ground, do not sink into it; low contacts in base phase

name: High-impact plyos (power day)
coaching_cues: Only when fresh; quality contacts over quantity; pair with the acceleration day, never the day before speed

name: Active recovery day
reps: easy jog 15-20 min + foam roll + static stretch
coaching_cues: Leave better than you arrived; this day is what makes the high days possible

name: Lactate tolerance ladder (short rest): 3 x 3 x 300m
rest: 30-45 sec between reps, 6 min between sets
coaching_cues: Short rest keeps lactate elevated on purpose; hold form as it builds; advanced seniors only - scale to 2 sets for younger athletes
source: Dunham USTFCCCA 2015 symposium (peak lactate tolerance, short rest)

name: Lactate peak reps (long rest): 2 x 300m
coaching_cues: Full recovery so each rep spikes to peak speed; just below top speed, not survival running; variants from the same menu: 2 x 400m or 2 x 200m
source: Dunham USTFCCCA 2015 symposium (peak lactate tolerance, long rest)

name: High-volume 100s at 400m pace
coaching_cues: Every rep at goal 400m pace, none faster; rhythm and relaxation are the session; stop if pace falls off

name: Tempo endurance 200s (400m group)
coaching_cues: Fast and relaxed, never strained; this is the aerobic bank deposit that pays for the last 100m of the 400

name: Over-distance special endurance: 2 x 600m
coaching_cues: Run it like a long 400: controlled first 400, then hold; over-distance makes 400 feel short

name: Special endurance 500s
coaching_cues: The Dunham-framework original the 100/200 plan cut: distribute effort, no sprinting the first 200; finish mechanics matter most
source: Dunham 400m framework (500m speed endurance in AJ plan source material)

name: Split run 480 (3 x 160m)
rest: 30 sec between segments, 10-12 min between sets
coaching_cues: Each 160 faster than 400m race pace (set from best 200m); 30 sec barely recovers half the phosphocreatine - that is the point; once per 10-day cycle, never within 2 days of a meet

name: Split run 320 (2 x 160m)
rest: 30 sec between segments, 8-10 min between sets
coaching_cues: The entry dose of split runs before the 480 version; segments above 400m race pace; teach athletes to re-accelerate on tired legs

name: Event run: 350m
coaching_cues: Race the first 300 exactly on the 400m model, then practise the finish; the last 50m is rehearsed, not endured

name: Broken 400: 300 fast + jog 100 + 100 fast
rest: jog 100m between segments, full between sets
coaching_cues: The closing 100 starts on tired legs like a real final; from the broken-run family in the AJ plan, extended to the full 400
source: AJ 100/200 plan, Phase 3 note (broken runs, 400m variant)

name: Differential 200s (first-200 pacing)
coaching_cues: Hit the target, not the max: first 200 of the 400 should be best open 200 plus about 1 sec (elite) to 2 sec (developing); teaches distribution, the skill the whole race hangs on

name: 400m-pace 300s (speed endurance, full recovery)
coaching_cues: 300m at goal 400m rhythm through 300; if the last 50 falls apart twice, the session is over; quality over completion
source: 400m extension - bridges AJ SE-03 distance up to 400m pace work

name: Standard sprint warm-up (full routine, 20-25 min)
coaching_cues: Part A: jog 800m + progressive strides and skipping series. Part B: dynamic series - leg swings, knee hugs, quad pulls, lunges with twist, inchworms, A-skips, B-skips, high knees, butt kicks, straight-leg bounds, karaoke, hip circles, ankle dribbles. Part C: 2-3 build-ups to session speed. Every session starts the same way.
source: AJ 100/200 plan warm-up protocol (Parts A-C); drills DRL-01 to DRL-16

name: Short pre-meet warm-up (12-15 min)
coaching_cues: Jog 400m, skipping series, pick 6 dynamic drills (leg swings, knee hugs, A-skips, B-skips, high knees, ankle dribbles), 2 progressive strides, 1-2 block starts. Finish 10 min before race time; stay moving and warm.
source: Trimmed from AJ warm-up protocol for meet days

name: Tempo-day warm-up (short, 10 min)
coaching_cues: Jog 400-800m easy, leg swings, knee hugs, quad pulls, ankle dribbles, 2 relaxed strides. Low days stay low - the warm-up should never become a workout.
source: Trimmed from AJ warm-up protocol for low days

name: Pool running (aqua jog intervals)
coaching_cues: Upright sprint posture in the water, quick turnover, drive the arms. Zero impact - the go-to swap when legs are beat up or a sprinter cannot run.

name: Bike tempo intervals
coaching_cues: Steady tempo effort, high cadence, relaxed shoulders. Builds the same aerobic base as tempo runs with no pounding.

name: Cross-train circuit rotation
coaching_cues: Rotate bike, rower, elliptical each round. Nasal breathing, conversational effort. A full low day without a single foot strike.

name: Mobility, core and mini-band day
coaching_cues: Hip mobility flow, mini-band walks and drills, core circuit, foam roll and stretch (static work belongs here, after training). The repair day - use it the day after the hardest session of the week.

name: Easy swim flush
coaching_cues: Easy laps, any stroke, never breathless. Flushes the legs and resets the nervous system after race weekends.
